title: Integrating Generative AI Tools into Cloud Native Applications
overview: Connect the Transformer’s attention mechanism to practical uses of language models. Compare a plain model call, retrieval-augmented generation and tool-using agents, then place them in the GenAI stack. Choose the simplest pattern that supplies the context or actions the application needs, with a clear business benefit.
big_ideas: Transformers enable parallel computation over training inputs with self-attention; autoregressive generation still produces tokens sequentially.
Self-attention uses Query, Key and Value vectors: compare a word's Query with every Key, softmax the scores into weights, and sum the weighted Values.
A plain LLM uses supplied context; RAG adds retrieved information; an agent selects steps or tools and can also use RAG.
An agent sits at the centre, using one or more LLMs plus integrations (tools, vector store, prompt recipes); frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex help build it.
Generative model families: encoder models (VAE), GANs, autoregressive, flow, energy-based and diffusion models.
Foundation models are pre-trained once on massive data (high cost, high performance) and then adapted by fine-tuning or prompt engineering.
GenAI tech stack: hardware, cloud platforms, foundation models, customisation, then end-to-end applications.
Business value: creativity, personalisation, faster answers, simplifying complex systems, automating admin, content at scale.

sections.title: From RNNs to Transformers
sections.summary: The short history that led to Transformers, contrasting the sequential RNN with the parallel, attention-based Transformer.
notes: **Transformers improve training parallelism and context handling.** RNNs propagate state step by step. Self-attention connects positions directly and allows parallel computation over known training inputs. An autoregressive Transformer still generates its output token by token; parallel training does not mean all future output tokens are known at once.

**Contrast the information path.** An RNN passes context through recurrent state; self-attention lets a position combine allowed context positions directly. This helps large-scale training and long-range relationships without guaranteeing perfect understanding.

The 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need introduced the Transformer. GPT means Generative Pretrained Transformer. GPT, Claude and Gemini are examples of model families, rather than a claim that one vendor’s model descended from another vendor’s product.

terms.def: Recurrent Neural Network: processes a sequence one step at a time, carrying state forward.
Neural network architecture (2017) that processes sequences in parallel using self-attention.
Generative Pretrained Transformer, the model family behind ChatGPT.

check.q: A team training a language model on a large corpus finds an RNN takes weeks because each step waits for the previous one. Why would a Transformer train faster on the same hardware?
check.a: An RNN passes context through recurrent state one step at a time, so training can't be parallelised across a sequence. Self-attention connects positions directly, so computation over the known training input can run in parallel, which suits GPU hardware. It also links distant words without passing through every step in between.

check.q: A colleague says 'Transformers process everything in parallel, so a chatbot built on one generates its whole answer at once'. Is that right?
check.a: No. Parallelism applies to training over known inputs. An autoregressive Transformer such as a GPT-style model still generates output token by token, each new token predicted from the context so far. That is why response time grows with answer length, and why streaming the output token by token is common in chat applications.

visuals.title: RNN vs Transformer
rows: Steps one after another; state carried from time step to time step
Parallel over known input positions; output generation remains autoregressive
Context travels through the recurrent state
Self-attention captures context and long-distance connections

sections.title: How self-attention works
sections.summary: Self-attention explained with a library analogy (Query, Key, Value) and a four-step computation giving each word a context-rich representation.
notes: **Self-attention lets each word build its meaning from the words that matter most to it.** Analogy: the Query is your question about the current word, the Keys are the labels of every other word you match against, and the Values are the content you collect from the best matches.

**Four steps per token:** form learned Query, Key and Value vectors; score the Query against allowed Keys; use softmax to obtain weights summing to 1; sum the weighted Values. The lecture illustrates 'it' attending more to 'animal' than 'street'. The numbers are explanatory examples, not fixed learned rules.

The result is a context-rich representation. Encoder self-attention can use a whole input; causal decoder attention masks future positions. Encoder-decoder models also use cross-attention to connect decoder queries with encoder outputs.

terms.def: Mechanism combining Value vectors using Query–Key relevance weights over allowed context positions.
Three learned vectors per word: the question, the label to match against, and the content to take.
Function that turns raw scores into weights that add up to 1.

check.q: In 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was tired', explain how self-attention gives 'it' the right meaning, and what would change in 'because it was too wide'.
check.a: The Query for 'it' is scored against every word's Key, softmax turns the scores into weights, and the weighted sum of Values gives 'it' a representation built mostly from 'animal'. In 'because it was too wide', the context changes the scores, so 'street' would get the higher weight. The weights are learned from data, not fixed rules.

check.q: What would go wrong if the attention scores were used directly as weights, without softmax?
check.a: Raw scores are on an arbitrary scale and can be negative, so the weighted sum of Values would not be a proper average and could be dominated by scale rather than relevance. Softmax turns the scores into positive weights that sum to 1, so the output is a weighted average that favours the best-matching words.

check.q: A text-generation model must not use words that come later in the sentence when predicting the next word, but a translation model's encoder can read the whole source sentence. How does attention differ between them?
check.a: A generating decoder uses causal attention, which masks future positions so each token attends only to earlier ones. An encoder's self-attention can use the whole input. Encoder-decoder models also use cross-attention, so the decoder's queries can look at the encoder's outputs.

steps.label: Create Q, K, V
steps.detail: Query = question, Key = label, Value = content.

steps.label: Score
steps.detail: Score this token’s Query against context Keys, respecting any mask that excludes future positions.

steps.label: Softmax
steps.detail: Weights sum to 1; e.g. 'it' gives 0.8 to 'animal', 0.05 to 'street'.

steps.label: Weighted sum
steps.detail: Result is a context-rich representation of the word.

sections.title: LLM vs RAG vs Agents, and what GenAI is
sections.summary: Three ways of using a language model (plain LLM, RAG, agent), the parts of an autonomous agent, and a definition of Generative AI.
notes: **Choose by missing information or action.** A plain LLM uses its learned parameters plus the supplied prompt/context; it does not inherently fetch current company data. RAG retrieves documents and adds them to that context. An agent can select tools and act over several steps, often also using retrieval. These patterns combine; they are not a compulsory ladder.

**The agent architecture combines an interface, model, instructions and integrations.** The lecture adds planning, tool access and memory/context, with a vector store as one retrieval option. Orchestration frameworks connect these pieces; persistent vector memory is not required for every tool-using agent.

**Generative AI** is the part of machine learning that learns the patterns and distribution of a training dataset and samples new, similar content from it (e.g. new owl images from random noise). Agentic AI goes further: it sets goals, plans, acts autonomously and adapts.

terms.def: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: fetch relevant context and give it to the LLM with the prompt.
An LLM-centred system that selects steps or tools to pursue a task; it can use retrieval and memory where needed.
Database of embeddings used to find semantically similar content for context and memory.
Orchestration frameworks for wiring LLMs to data, memory and tools.

check.q: An HR chatbot built on a plain LLM call gives confident but outdated answers about this year's leave policy. Which pattern fixes this, and why not retrain the model?
check.a: RAG: retrieve the current policy documents and add them to the prompt, so answers are grounded in the company's own, up-to-date data. A plain LLM only knows its training data plus the prompt. Retraining is costly and goes stale again with the next policy change, whereas updating the document index is cheap. Keep the index current, because RAG is only as fresh as its sources.

check.q: A RAG assistant retrieves the refund policy correctly. The business now wants it to issue refunds as well. What changes in the design, and what new risk appears?
check.a: It becomes an agent: the model selects tools, such as calling the order and payment service APIs, and acts over several steps, still using retrieval for policy. The new risk is that retrieval gave the model information, not permission. Each tool needs authorisation checks, limits such as a refund cap, and logging, with human approval for high-value actions.

check.q: A team building an agent that calls two internal APIs says it must first set up a vector store for memory. Is that required?
check.a: No. The lecture's agent architecture has an interface, a model, instructions or a prompt recipe, planning, tool integrations and memory or context, and a vector store is one retrieval option. A tool-using agent with short tasks may need only conversation context. Add a vector store when the agent must retrieve from a large document set.

check.q: A RAG assistant cites a company document but still gives a wrong answer. Give two likely causes and how you would confirm each.
check.a: Retrieval may have returned a stale or irrelevant passage: check the retrieved chunks and their dates. Or the model misread correct context: check whether the answer is actually supported by the retrieved text. Retrieval is not a correctness guarantee, so evaluate retrieval quality and answer support separately.

steps.label: User question
steps.detail: Define the information need; the model does not automatically know private or current documents.

steps.label: Retrieve passages
steps.detail: Find context in an appropriate authorised source; retrieval quality limits what evidence is available.

steps.label: Assemble prompt
steps.detail: Supply selected passages alongside the question. This changes context without changing model weights.

steps.label: Generate answer
steps.detail: The LLM uses the prompt and its learned patterns. Check that the answer is actually supported; retrieval alone does not guarantee correctness.

sections.title: Model families, value and the GenAI stack
sections.summary: Six families of generative models, why businesses want GenAI services, and foundation models with the layered GenAI tech stack.
notes: **Six families of generative model, each generating differently:** variational autoencoders (VAEs) compress and decode data; GANs pit a generator against a discriminator; autoregressive models predict the next value from previous ones (how LLMs write text); flow models transform simple distributions into complex ones; energy-based models give low energy to real data and high to others; diffusion models learn to reverse a defined noise-adding process. GAN vs diffusion: adversarial competition vs reversing gradual noising.
**Why businesses want GenAI services:** creativity, smart suggestions, personalisation, instant answers, simplifying complex systems with plain language, automating admin work, and content at scale.

**Foundation models are pre-trained once, at high cost, on massive broad data, then adapted** (fine-tuning, prompt engineering) to many tasks such as Q&A, extraction, captioning and instruction following.

**GenAI tech stack, bottom up:** hardware (GPUs/TPUs), cloud platforms (scalable compute, storage, AI services), foundation models (closed via API, or open-weight with released parameters), customisation, then end-to-end applications. Closed vs open: closed is ready to use but ties you to a provider; released weights can allow self-hosting and tuning under their licence, at the cost of operating the model.

terms.def: Generative Adversarial Network: a generator and discriminator trained against each other.
Learns to reverse a noise-adding process, generating data by gradually denoising.
Large model pre-trained on massive broad data, adapted to many downstream tasks.
Platform to share and host models, e.g. Hugging Face.
Further training a pre-trained model on domain data to specialise it.

check.q: A design team wants a model that generates realistic product images, and is comparing a GAN with a diffusion model. Explain how each generates, as the basis for the comparison.
check.a: A GAN trains a generator against a discriminator that tries to tell real images from generated ones, and generates in one pass from the trained generator. A diffusion model learns to reverse a defined noise-adding process, and generates by progressively denoising a random sample over many steps. So the comparison is between adversarial training and iterative denoising.

check.q: A hospital must keep patient text inside its own environment, but wants to summarise clinical notes with a language model. Closed model through an API, or open-weight model self-hosted?
check.a: An open-weight model self-hosted in the hospital's environment fits the data constraint: the released weights allow deployment and tuning under their licence without sending notes to a provider. The cost is operating GPUs, capacity, updates and reliability. A closed API is ready to use but ties you to the provider and sends data outside, unless its terms and deployment options meet the constraint.

check.q: A startup plans to train its own foundation model for customer-support answers. What does the GenAI stack suggest instead?
check.a: Foundation models are expensive to pre-train but reusable across many tasks. Most teams add value higher up the stack: customisation through prompt engineering, RAG or fine-tuning, and the end-to-end application. Training their own model is justified only for a capability or a data constraint that existing models can't meet.

layers.label: End-to-end applications
layers.detail: User-facing apps with proprietary AI models (e.g. Midjourney, Runway, ActiveChat.AI).

layers.label: Customisation
layers.detail: Fine-tuning, prompt engineering and adaptation for domain-specific use cases.

layers.label: Foundation models
layers.detail: Broadly pretrained models can be consumed through an API or deployed from released weights where permitted. Weight availability and open-source licensing are separate questions.

layers.label: Cloud platforms
layers.detail: Google Cloud, AWS, Azure (also CoreWeave): scalable compute, storage and AI services over virtualised infrastructure.

layers.label: Hardware
layers.detail: GPUs, TPUs, servers and accelerator chips for AI training and inference.

sections.title: Key applications and use cases
sections.summary: GenAI application areas, with concrete business use cases for voice, video, text and music generation.
notes: **GenAI generates many media types:** voice, video, text and translation, music, images, 3D objects, generative design, and scientific uses such as protein folding. For an architect each is a capability consumed as a service through APIs.

**Voice and text** target service and knowledge work: AI phone agents and IVR that cut wait times, multilingual and accessible narration, auto-generated FAQs and chatbot answers, translation, and first drafts of proposals and reports.

**Video and music** target marketing and media: personalised videos per segment, virtual presenters for training, product visualisation before manufacture, lip-synced localisation without reshooting, brand jingles, adaptive soundtracks and ad tracks where the applicable usage terms permit.
**Common business value:** content at scale, personalisation, lower cost and faster delivery.

terms.def: Interactive Voice Response: automated phone menu systems.

check.q: A bank wants to cut call-centre wait times with GenAI. Which application fits, and what must be added for it to be accurate?
check.a: An AI phone agent: speech interaction combined with a language-model service that handles routine enquiries. Voice generation alone is not enough. Answers must come from maintained knowledge sources (RAG), and account actions need authorised tools, with handoff to a human for complex or sensitive cases.

check.q: A marketing team wants lip-synced localised versions of a training video in 12 languages, plus a brand jingle. What does the architect need to check before treating these as simple API calls?
check.a: Quality review for each language, since translation and lip-sync errors are public, and the usage and licence terms for generated voice, likeness and music. Consider cost and turnaround at scale too. Each capability can be consumed as a service through APIs, but the workflow needs a human approval step before publication.

exam_angles.q: Design a GenAI customer-support assistant for a cloud-native e-commerce platform that must answer from current product and policy documents and also check order status. Choose plain LLM, RAG or agent, and say how it fits into the existing microservices.
exam_angles.a: Use RAG for answers, retrieving current product docs, FAQs and policies from an index such as a vector store, so responses are grounded without retraining. Extend it to an agent with tools for order status, calling the order service's existing API with the customer's own authorisation, and keep refunds behind human approval. Run the assistant as its own service behind the API gateway, using a hosted foundation model through an API or a self-hosted open-weight model. Monitor retrieval quality and answer support, because retrieval doesn't guarantee correctness.

exam_angles.q: Explain the layers of the GenAI tech stack, and advise a 10-person cloud-native team on where to invest and where to buy.
exam_angles.a: Bottom up: hardware (GPUs/TPUs), cloud platforms (scalable compute, storage, AI services), foundation models (closed through an API, or open-weight), customisation (prompt engineering, RAG, fine-tuning), and end-to-end applications. Buy the bottom three: pre-training is high-cost and existing models are reusable. Invest in customisation and the application, where the team's data and domain knowledge create value. Choose closed versus open weights by data constraints and operating capacity.

exam_angles.q: An enterprise wants GenAI for expense processing: answer staff questions about the policy, read receipt images and submit claims. Compare a plain LLM, RAG and an agent for this, and design the safeguards for the part that acts.
exam_angles.a: A plain LLM can interpret text but doesn't know the company's current policy. RAG adds the retrieved policy, which is enough for staff questions. Extracting receipt data and submitting claims needs an agent with tools calling the expense system's API. Safeguards: tools act only with the employee's permissions, limits route claims above a threshold to human approval, every action is logged, and the agent can only prepare or submit within defined integrations. The patterns combine, but an answer is not a permitted business action.

exam_angles.q: A product manager asks why chat responses get slower as answers get longer, even though 'Transformers are parallel'. Explain using the RNN-to-Transformer change, and give one design implication for a cloud-native chat service.
exam_angles.a: Transformers replaced step-by-step recurrence with self-attention, which lets training run in parallel over known inputs and links distant context directly. That is what made large-scale training possible. Generation is still autoregressive: each token is predicted from the tokens so far, so a longer answer takes longer to generate. Design implication: stream tokens to the client as they are generated, and set timeouts and capacity by expected output length.

exam_angles.q: A global marketing organisation proposes three GenAI features: personalised video per customer segment, first-draft product copy in 8 languages, and AI-generated ad music. Assess each for business value and risk, and say what process control is needed across all three.
exam_angles.a: Personalised video increases engagement at scale, but it is the costliest to generate and carries the most likeness and brand risk. Multilingual draft copy gives the clearest time saving, with translation errors as the main risk. Ad music is cheap content at scale, but its usage terms must permit commercial use. The common business value is content at scale, personalisation and faster delivery. Across all three, require human review and approval before publication, and track the usage terms of each generated asset.
